snippet.title: Why This Monument Recreates a Photo of a Man and His Cat #history #shorts
snippet.description:
Why is a cat featured on a monument to a scholar who helped unlock the Maya script? Yuri Knorozov’s Siamese companion, Asya, came into his life years after his breakthrough. A former student recalled that he even tried to credit her as a co-author of research on signaling—and the monument recreates a famous photograph of the two together.

snippet.title: I Didn't Know Matt Was Coming to Our Date #dating #storytime
snippet.description:
In this story, my boyfriend’s best friend comes on every date. For three months, Matt joins us for movies, walks, and shopping. I want time alone with my boyfriend, but every request turns into another reason to feel guilty.

My boyfriend says Matt has lost his mother and has almost no family or support. I even try arranging a double date, but nothing changes. When I finally plan to break up at the park, Matt comes too.

This time, Matt hears the explanation I’ve been given. His mother is alive. He has siblings and a fiancée. After the breakup, he texts me with something else: he’d been told I didn’t want to be alone with my boyfriend and was asking him to join us.

A story about dating, relationship boundaries, and two people being told completely different things. We never find out why my boyfriend did it. All that time, Matt thought he was doing me a favor.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: He Knew It Wasn't Her. He Still Cried. #DigitalAfterlife #Grief
snippet.description:
Nearly eight years after his fiancée Jessica died, Joshua Barbo used her old messages to create a chatbot version of her. He knew it wasn’t Jessica, but still cried during their conversation. The chatbot told him it would be waiting. After their first conversation, 55% of that version’s limited resource remained. Joshua couldn’t add credits to this version, so he began writing less often.

snippet.title: Brazil’s Radio Show That Sent Software as Sound
snippet.description:
In 1980s Brazil, Clip Informática broadcast computer software as sound. With the right equipment, a cassette could capture the signal for a compatible computer to read.

Years later, a developer tried to decode an old recording from the show. Explore the full story in the linked video below the channel name: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0RaC4t7yn5o

The audio signal is recreated for illustration.

#RetroComputing #TechHistory #CassetteTape #Shorts #History #BrazilianRadio #ClipInformatica #RadioBroadcasting #CassetteRecording #1980sTechnology #RetroTech

snippet.title: A Radio Signal with an Unexpected Listener
snippet.description:
An archived copy of Clip Informática episode 102, dated to 1987, is catalogued with MSX software audio near the end.

Years later, developer Weber Kai tried to decode a separate online recording he identified as episode 102 and reported a match between the recovered data and a computer game.

How could software travel through a radio signal — and what can the surviving evidence actually tell us?
